summary: Generates irregular non-repeating noise channels, including smooth noise, random per-sample noise, and optional 3D noise-space sampling from input coordinates.

key_params.name: type
key_params.note: Noise function: sparse, hermite, harmonic, brownian, random, or alligator

key_params.name: seed
key_params.note: Random seed for distinct noise patterns

key_params.name: period
key_params.note: Approximate separation between peaks in the selected period unit

key_params.name: periodunit
key_params.note: Units for Period: samples, frames, seconds, or fraction

key_params.name: harmon
key_params.note: Number of higher-frequency harmonics layered over the base frequency

key_params.name: spread
key_params.note: Frequency multiplier between harmonics for Harmonic Summation

key_params.name: exp
key_params.note: Exponent shaping that pulls values toward zero or peaks

key_params.name: numint
key_params.note: Number of integrations for Random noise

key_params.name: amp
key_params.note: Amplitude scale applied to output values

key_params.name: reset
key_params.note: Reset and hold time-sliced noise while active

key_params.name: xord
key_params.note: Transform order for sampling the 3D noise space

key_params.name: rord
key_params.note: Rotate order for sampling the 3D noise space

key_params.name: constraint
key_params.note: Optional start, end, mean, or endpoint constraints

key_params.name: normal
key_params.note: Normalize selected noise types before amplitude

key_params.name: autoexportroot
key_params.note: Root path for automatic channel-name exports

key_params.name: exporttable
key_params.note: DAT table used by DAT table export methods

key_concepts: Noise CHOP generates an irregular wave that never repeats and is approximately in the -1 to 1 range before amplitude scaling.
It can generate smooth curves or random per-sample white noise.
Noise shape is controlled by type, seed, period, amplitude, harmonics, roughness, exponent, and integration count.
An optional input can provide one to three X/Y/Z coordinate channels used to sample 3D noise space.
Translate, rotate, scale, and pivot parameters change where and how the 3D noise field is sampled.
Time Slice mode works for most noise functions but has documented exceptions for Harmonic Summation and Brownian settings.
common_gotchas: The official roughness parameter id is rough, not roughness.
Period should be greater than zero except Random noise with period zero.
Harmonic Spread only applies to Harmonic Summation.
Harmonic detail requires both Harmonics and Roughness to be nonzero.
Constraint and Normalize options work only when Time Slice is Off.
Reset and Reset Pulse are only available when Time Slice is On.
